question: F16: the sine-phase endpoint is reported with no amplitude-identifiability rule. Is the phase identifiable when the fitted amplitude is near the noise level, and what rule should govern its reporting?

cold_axis_definitions.cold_window_overlap: share of the station's climatological coldest-30-day window (estimated from every year but the target year) that the outage hides; exact mirror of the stored peak_overlap column
cold_axis_definitions.cold_season_observed_fraction: observed share of the non-warm calendar months (Oct-Apr); exact algebraic function of stored total_missing, missing_fraction and warm_observed_fraction

cold_window_wander.note: raw doy sd is inflated by the 31 December wrap; circular sd is the honest figure

estimator_guard_evidence: sine_parameters returns sine_phase whenever at least 30 finite days are present and the least-squares solve succeeds; abserr_sine_phase is then computed unconditionally. No amplitude or signal-to-noise test exists in endpoints.py, in the v18 e3 runner, or in the manuscript's sine table.

phase_tolerance.tolerance_rule: 0.4717 of the phase's interannual sd (step 17 convention)

noise_scale_bracket.primary: sine_resid_sd_observed (residual sd of the fit to the days actually present)
noise_scale_bracket.sensitivity: sine_resid_sd_truth (residual sd of the same fit to the complete year)
noise_scale_bracket.note: the repaired series is smoother than the observed days alone, so its own residual sd lies between these two; they bracket the rule's input to within a few per cent

reporting_rule.form: report the sine-fit phase only when the fitted amplitude exceeds k times the residual sd
reporting_rule.derivation: the phase standard error of a three-parameter sine fit is se(phi) = sigma*sqrt(2/n)/A radians, so requiring a 95% interval no wider than the study's own phase tolerance tau gives A/sigma >= 2*sqrt(2/n)/tau
